hypothesis: WriterGuard::drop's unconditional notify_one is a futex_wake syscall per write txn on Linux; LMDB avoids it with a pthread me_wmutex that only enters the kernel under contention; a waiter count under the flag mutex makes ZeroDB notify only when a writer is parked.

hypothesis: GC draws hand out the smallest id with Vec::drain(0..1), an O(L) memmove per page, so draining one entry is O(L^2); LMDB pops from the tail of a reverse-sorted me_pghead; a head offset per drain entry makes the front pop O(1) with byte-identical GC-20 output.

Those rungs never drain a large entry, so the logic is unchanged there; nm shows allocate shrank 4276 -> 3801 B and commit grew 8782 -> 9165 B, i.e. codegen/layout of the write path moved. Gate was fully green (95 test bins, crash-test, stress, miri, fuzz). Patch kept at benches-server/research/attempt-1a-gc-head-offset.patch. Retry after the #8 codegen gate (e.g. #[inline(never)] on the GC draw so the hot allocate path keeps its old shape), measured at CGU1 and CGU16.

Evidence for the next lever, from nm of the codegen-gate builds (CGU1 vs CGU1+inline-threshold=1000): inlined away at threshold 1000 are heed_zerodb::Database::get, node_view, Source::bytes_from_classified, ValidatedPages::contains, BranchRef::child_index_with, Cursor::leaf_at, read_and_check_bounds, OverflowRef::new, leaf_cell_len. hypothesis: The write-path descent's heap Vec path (malloc/free/grow ~3 % of put/val/v8) is avoidable; LMDB's mdb_put descends with a stack cursor (fixed CURSOR_STACK array); using btree::PathStack (inline, 32 frames) in search_path/rightmost_path does the same.

hypothesis: A fresh descent-path Vec per put/delete (alloc+grow+free, ~3 % of put/val/v8) is avoidable; LMDB allocates its cursor stack once and reuses it; one per-txn path buffer (mem::take/restore) does the same without the 520 B init/copy that sank the inline-PathStack try.

hypothesis: Every first-touch COW and new page mallocs a fresh 4 KiB Box and every freed/committed frame is freed; LMDB reuses dirty-page buffers via me_dpages within and across txns; a spare-frame list in DirtyStore plus a cross-txn pool (capped at 256 frames, since ZeroDB has no spill) does the same.
notes: Gains real in both builds: put/gc/drain_big 1.62x -> 1.23x (0.76-0.79), put/val/v4k 1.04x -> 1.00x, commit/batch/n1 -3 % at CGU1; target commit/batch/n1 otherwise flat (its +2.3 us is the copy, not the malloc). Reverted for env/txn/rw_empty_commit: v1 (per-frame pool hand-over) 6.1x slower; v2 (O(1) hand-over, separate Mutex) +36 %; v3 (pool under the writer-slot mutex, zero extra lock ops) CGU16 flat but CGU1 +15.3 % over 5 rounds (ab-20260927T010700Z, +-0.098, layout-offset flag). Remaining per-txn work is a few Vec moves + the new Drop for RwTxn; unproven whether code or layout. Patch (v3): attempt-3b-frame-pool.patch. Human call: a ~25 ns/empty-txn cost vs -24 % on GC-heavy writes.
